keys.beat: Menelaus answers with the story of the wooden horse.
keys.text: 'What endurance too, and what courage he displayed within the wooden horse, wherein all the bravest of the Argives were lying in wait to bring death and destruction upon the Trojans.'

keys.beat: Helen circled the horse and imitated the voices of the warriors' wives.
keys.text: 'Three times did you go all round our hiding place and pat it with your hands, calling our chiefs each by his own name, and mimicking all our wives.'

keys.beat: The hidden Greeks nearly answered; Odysseus restrained them and silenced Anticlus.
keys.text: 'Diomed, myself, and the son of Tydeus who were inside heard what a noise you made, and would have gone out; but Ulysses held us back... Anticlus alone would have answered you, but Ulysses kept his hands pressed firmly over his mouth.'

keys.beat: Telemachus hears proof of his father's endurance and command under pressure.
keys.text: 'He kept his hands pressed firmly over his mouth till Minerva took you away again.'
